issue_context.title: Allow Consolidator Reset
issue_context.body:
#### Expected Behavior
It is possible to reset consolidators.
Say we have a weekly or monthly consolidator, and a split occurs. The weekly/monthly bar will have pre- and post-split data:

![Captura de ecrã 2024-09-11 231322](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/680929b4-4de1-442b-bf53-56b31ec9b661)

We can workaround this issue by removing the consolidator from the subscription_manager, and create a new one.

```python
    def reset_consolidator(self, symbol):
        self.subscription_manager.remove_consolidator(symbol, self.consolidator)
        self.consolidator: TradeBarConsolidator = self.consolidate(symbol, Calendar.WEEKLY, self.on_weekly_bar)
```

Ideally, this should be a simple `reset` method call as supported by indicators. 

#### Actual Behavior
We cannot reset indicators. 

#### Potential Solution
Add `Reset` method that sets the internal working data to null.

#### Reproducing the Problem
[backtest #c52d5e](https://www.quantconnect.com/terminal/processCache?request=embedded_backtest_c52d5eabb58016b042a2f5a65072314a.html)

review_comments: Could be directly null, it's the default for all posible T types.
Hmm perhaps it was the rule for previous versions of .NET but apparently now is not the case: https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/csharp/misc/cs0403?f1url=%3FappId%3Droslyn%26k%3Dk(CS0403)

Just a thought but maybe in order to keep this private, you could have an abstract protected `ResetConsolidator()` for derived clases to implement and a public non-virtual `Reset()` that calls `ResetConsolidator` and set `Consolidated` to null?

It could be, but there are other abstract consolidators doing the same (making `Consolidated` protected) like BaseTimelessConsolidator https://github.com/QuantConnect/Lean/blob/master/Common/Data/Consolidators/BaseTimelessConsolidator.cs#L54
